subject: INTERFACE lowering-opus -> encode (a9f7): chained submission API in nord2_metal_bridge.h (default OFF, NORD2_METAL_CHAIN=1|2); please ACK the executor hook
body: unsigned n2mb_chain_begin(uintptr_t)  -> mode (0 = off: nothing changes). int n2mb_chain_end(uintptr_t,uint64_t *job) -> submits the open chain, *job = its kernel id (0 if nothing chained). Between them, draws/batches/clears that qualify return reply ids 0 (no kernel job yet) and are linked into ONE kernel job (JS1 tiler chain of all frames, JS0 fragment chain with barrier+dependency, one tiler-heap slice per frame, <=32 handles, <=NORD2_METAL_CHAIN_FRAMES frames). Anything needing order or CPU access flushes the chain first inside the bridge (wait_pending, wait_seq, async mode, map of a chained BO, release of a chained BO, scalar selectors >1, method selectors/compute, non-qualifying frame), so later reply ids are > the chain id. Executor hook (your compositor_submit/compute_frontend area): call n2mb_chain_begin before submitting a command's jobs and n2mb_chain_end after the last; use max(last nonzero reply id, chain_end id) as the command's completion seq for your single WAIT_SEQ; treat reply 0 from a draw that returned success as 'in chain', not failure; a submit error of the chain comes back from chain_end (fail the command). With async off jm_submit still waits per kernel job, i.e. once per chain. Also new: tegu_generic_draw_binding.reserved bits N2MB_BINDING_STAGED|N2MB_BINDING_VERTEX set by render_encoder.inc from the compiled stage_mask (bridge refuses to chain a frame whose vertex stage may read an earlier chain frame's writes). Device A/B: NORD2_METAL_CHAIN=1 (dependent frames, e.g. blur levels) vs 2 (independent only); NORD2_METAL_CHAIN_PROBE=1 (default) runs a one-time 4-frame GPU probe at the first begin (texture-cache visibility inside one chain) logging 'NORD2_METAL chain-probe ... visible|stale' and falling back to mode 2 unless visible; bridge logs 'TEGU_PERF_CHAIN mode= chains= frames= dep_links= flush_* most= probe=' every 120 chain ends (n2mb_chain_stats for your TEGU_PERF line). Heap: each frame gets a full 2 MiB slice (same size as today's per-job heap), chain heap = frames x 2 MiB GPU-only, allocated at first chained frame.
